title: Coarse information and finite rank obstructions for flat lattice Hodge forms
abstract: For finite flat lattice component-gradient forms we study the dimension and geometry of coarse observations needed for coercivity. The principal constructive theorem selects a coefficient-only partition into integer rectangles for every positive scalar coefficient in dimension D>=3. Actual normalized means, with penalty K=c, give a uniform all-field lower bound, and a full inverse D/2 moment yields the target-order output dimension including D(Nc^2-1) real components. The proof derives an unweighted balanced-ring BV extension, applies original-start weighted Holder estimates and compresses coefficient-mass trees while retaining within-ring interfaces. Odd sizes, singleton directions, atomic heavy mass and complete cover/count are treated. Earlier Fourier and critical spectral bounds, exact Schur penalty specializations and counterexamples distinguish successful observations from failed sufficient certificates. Classical BV, approximation, Fourier, Schur and resistance mechanisms are attributed; historical priority of the finite specialization remains unestablished. The result is analytic finite scalar-gradient mathematics, not a general matrix rectangular theorem, an interacting coefficient producer, a variable-weight curl identity, a continuum construction or a physical mass gap. Separately scoped formal endpoints and selected finite diagnostics do not certify the entire manuscript. The exact101-page working paper has one numerical AI assessment with full report, adverse findings and involved-reviewer context retained.
